# PART II — BUILD PHASE

## 2.0 Pre-flight (do these before Hour 0; ~45 min, can overlap)

**People first.** The binding constraint is your friends, not code. **Right now**, before you open an editor, message your group:

> "Experiment this weekend: I'm building a bot that plans one short outing for us and nags us so it actually happens. Sunday morning, 2–3 hours, close by. Can you do Sunday morning? If yes, I'll add you to a Telegram group tonight. It only reads messages you send *to it* (commands/replies), and you can `/forget` yourself any time."

Then export your existing group chat (WhatsApp: *More → Export chat → Without media*; Telegram Desktop: *Export chat history*). Count the real phrase:

```bash
grep -ciE "we should|let'?s (go|do|plan)" chat.txt   # → {{WE_SHOULD_COUNT}}
grep -iE "we should" chat.txt | head -1               # first date → {{SINCE_DATE}}
```

Ask the group whether you may quote that number and two of their messages. Then create the accounts, verifying "no card" on each:

| # | Account / install | Card? | Verified source |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | GitHub repo `quorum` (public, **Apache-2.0**) | No | — |
| 2 | Google AI Studio API key (`GOOGLE_API_KEY`). Gemma 4 is "Free of charge"; Paid Tier "Not available" | No (free tier) | [Gemini pricing](https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/pricing) |
| 3 | MongoDB Atlas **M0** cluster, a DB user, Network Access `0.0.0.0/0` (Render has no static IP on Free) | Not stated on the official page. Stop if asked | [M0 limits](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/reference/free-shared-limitations/) |
| 4 | Render account (GitHub login), Free web service | No ("If you haven't added a payment method…") | [Render Free](https://render.com/docs/free) |
| 5 | Telegram bot via **@BotFather** `/newbot` → `TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN`. **Leave privacy mode ON** | No | [Telegram privacy mode](https://core.telegram.org/bots/features#privacy-mode) |
| 6 | Temporal CLI (`brew install temporal`, or the Linux/Windows binary from the Temporal CLI docs) | No (OSS) | [Temporal CLI server](https://docs.temporal.io/cli/server) |
| 7 | Entire CLI: `curl -fsSL https://entire.io/install.sh \| bash` (macOS: `brew install --cask entireio/tap/entire`) | No (MIT) | [Entire quickstart](https://docs.entire.io/quickstart.md) |
| 8 | Node 22 LTS, `npm`, optionally Ollama + `ollama pull gemma4:e4b` (6.6–9.5 GB) for the local comparison | No | [Ollama gemma4](https://ollama.com/library/gemma4) |
| 9 | *(stretch)* SerpApi key. Free = 250 searches/month, 50/hour | Not stated. Stop if asked | [SerpApi pricing](https://serpapi.com/pricing) |
| 10 | Promos: log in at [hacktoberfest.com/my/promos](https://hacktoberfest.com/my/promos) and claim the Render promo if one is offered. Not required; Free tier suffices | — | [Challenge page](https://dev.to/challenges/hacktoberfest-week1-2026-10-05) |

**Fallback decision made up front:** if Atlas asks for a card → §2.6 "Atlas". If Render asks for a card → §2.6 "Render". If neither asks, proceed.

## 2.1 Stack

| Layer | Choice | Why (and why not the alternative) |
|---|---|---|
| Language | TypeScript, Node 22 | Mastra and the Temporal TS SDK are both TypeScript-native. One language for agent, workflow and bot |
| Agent framework | **Mastra** (`@mastra/core`, `@mastra/memory`, `@mastra/mongodb`), Apache-2.0 | Agents, tools, memory and an HTTP server in one package ([Mastra agents](https://mastra.ai/docs/agents/overview); [pricing/licence](https://mastra.ai/pricing)). Not LangChain: no first-class MongoDB memory with semantic recall in one config object |
| Model | **Gemma 4**: `google/gemma-4-31b-it` via the Gemini API free tier; `gemma4:e4b` via Ollama locally | Open weights, $0, and the same agent swaps to local. Gemma 4 has "built-in function-calling support" ([Gemma 4 overview](https://ai.google.dev/gemma/docs/core)). Not a closed API: the group's private facts would have no local option |
| Durability | **Temporal** OSS dev server + TS worker on your laptop | `temporal server start-dev --db-filename …` persists state; the Web UI is at :8233 ([Temporal CLI](https://docs.temporal.io/cli/server)). Not Temporal Cloud (needs a card, [pricing](https://temporal.io/pricing)). Not cron/`setTimeout` (dies on restart) |
| Memory / DB | **MongoDB Atlas M0** (512 MB, 100 ops/s, 500 connections, **max 3 search/vector indexes**) | [M0 limits](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/reference/free-shared-limitations/); "3 indexes (regardless of the type, `search` or `vector`) on Free clusters" ([Vector Search limitations](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/vector-search/deployment/compatibility-limitations/)) |
| Embeddings | `google/gemini-embedding-001` (768-d) via Mastra's `ModelRouterEmbeddingModel` | [Mastra embeddings](https://mastra.ai/models/embeddings). Same key as Gemma. Fallback: `@mastra/fastembed` (local) |
| Host | **Render Free web service** running `mastra build` output | The only host that is also a prize category. Free sleeps after 15 idle min and takes ~1 min to wake ([Render Free](https://render.com/docs/free)), which the design turns into a feature |
| Chat channel | **Telegram Bot API**, long polling from your laptop | Free and instant (BotFather), no public webhook or tunnel needed (`getUpdates` long polling), and native non-anonymous polls send per-voter `poll_answer` updates. Privacy mode means the bot only sees commands and replies addressed to it ([Bot API](https://core.telegram.org/bots/api)). Discord would also work (free) but needs a gateway client and has no per-voter poll update as simple as this. WhatsApp is out (business verification, paid) |
| Weather | Open-Meteo (no key; free for non-commercial use; 10,000 calls/day) | [Open-Meteo pricing](https://open-meteo.com/en/pricing) |
| Places | OSM Overpass API (public instance: ~10,000 requests/day, <1 GB/day) | [Overpass commons](https://dev.overpass-api.de/overpass-doc/en/preface/commons.html) |
| Live check *(stretch)* | SerpApi Google engine, cached in Atlas | [SerpApi pricing](https://serpapi.com/pricing) |
| Session history | **Entire CLI** with the **branch** checkpoint backend | Judges can browse `entire/checkpoints/v1` on GitHub without an Entire account (inferred; see §2.2) |

## 2.2 Verified build facts and the report's open questions, resolved

Checked against primary docs on 2026-10-09. ⚠ = not verified end-to-end. Your Hour-2 gate tests it.

| Question | Answer | Source |
|---|---|---|
| **Does Gemma 4 do tool/function calling?** | **Yes, natively.** Gemma 4 lists "built-in function-calling support". The chat template has dedicated tool tokens (`<\|tool_call>call:name{…}<tool_call\|>`) | [Gemma 4 overview](https://ai.google.dev/gemma/docs/core); [Gemma function calling](https://ai.google.dev/gemma/docs/capabilities/function-calling) |
| …via the **Gemini API**? | **Yes.** The Gemini API "supports the following Gemma 4 models: `gemma-4-31b-it` and `gemma-4-26b-a4b-it`". Function declarations work as with Gemini ("The model decides when to call them"). System instructions are supported. **Structured output / JSON mode is not documented for Gemma** there | [Gemma on Gemini API](https://ai.google.dev/gemma/docs/core/gemma_on_gemini_api?hl=en) |
| …via **Ollama**? | **Yes.** The `gemma4` library page carries the **tools** badge. Tags: `e2b`, `e4b`, `12b`, `26b`, `31b` | [Ollama gemma4](https://ollama.com/library/gemma4) |
| …in a way **Mastra** can use? | **Probably, but unproven ⚠.** Mastra's model router lists `google/gemma-4-31b-it` and `google/gemma-4-26b-a4b-it` (key `GOOGLE_API_KEY`), but its **Tools column for both is blank**. Mastra does not advertise tool support for them. Ollama works through an AI SDK community provider (`ollama-ai-provider-v2`). The AI SDK docs point to the alternative `ai-sdk-ollama` package for "reliable tool calling". A user reported Gemma 4 tool calls via Ollama not being recognised in **streaming** mode through the AI SDK OpenAI-compatible provider. **Decision:** use `generate()` (non-streaming). Run the 20-prompt smoke test at Gate 1 (§2.4). If validity is below 16/20, switch to the **prefetch fallback**: code runs the tools and Gemma only reasons and returns JSON. That keeps Gemma, Mastra and memory | [Mastra Google provider](https://mastra.ai/models/providers/google); [Mastra Ollama](https://mastra.ai/models/providers/ollama); [AI SDK Ollama](https://ai-sdk.dev/providers/community-providers/ollama); [OpenCode issue #20995](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/issues/20995) |
| Structured output with tools | Use `structuredOutput: { schema, jsonPromptInjection: true }`. Mastra documents that some models "can't combine structured output with tools". For Gemini 2.5 with tools, `jsonPromptInjection: true` is required. Assume the same for Gemma. Read `response.object` | [Mastra structured output](https://mastra.ai/docs/agents/structured-output) |
| Mastra agent API | `new Agent({ id, name, instructions, model: 'provider/model', tools, memory })` from `@mastra/core/agent`. `createTool({ id, description, inputSchema, outputSchema, execute: async (input, ctx) => … })` from `@mastra/core/tools`. `agent.generate(msg, { memory: { resource, thread }, maxSteps, structuredOutput, toolChoice })` returns `text, object, toolCalls, toolResults, steps, usage` | [Agents](https://mastra.ai/docs/agents/overview); [createTool](https://mastra.ai/reference/tools/create-tool); [generate()](https://mastra.ai/reference/agents/generate) |
| Mastra memory on MongoDB | `@mastra/mongodb` provides `MongoDBStore({ id, uri, dbName })` and `MongoDBVector({ id, uri, dbName })`. Semantic recall = `options.semanticRecall: { topK, messageRange, scope: 'resource' }` plus `vector` and `embedder`. MongoDB supports `scope: 'resource'`. Working memory exists but is updated through an `updateWorkingMemory` **tool call**. Quorum therefore keeps the roster in its own collection, so roster updates don't depend on Gemma tool calls | [MongoDB storage](https://mastra.ai/reference/storage/mongodb); [MongoDB vector](https://mastra.ai/reference/vectors/mongodb); [Semantic recall](https://mastra.ai/docs/memory/semantic-recall); [Working memory](https://mastra.ai/docs/memory/working-memory) |
| Mastra server on Render | `mastra build` → `.mastra/output/index.mjs`. Start with `node .mastra/output/index.mjs`. `PORT` overrides 4111. **Host defaults to `localhost`**, so set `MASTRA_HOST=0.0.0.0` on Render. `GET /health` returns 200. Custom routes via `registerApiRoute` from `@mastra/core/server`; handlers get a Hono context with `c.get('mastra')` | [Mastra server](https://mastra.ai/docs/deployment/mastra-server); [Config](https://mastra.ai/reference/configuration); [Custom routes](https://mastra.ai/docs/server/custom-api-routes) |
| Temporal timers | `sleep('5s')`, `sleep(ms)`. "Timers are persisted, so even if your Worker or Temporal Service is down…" the sleep resolves when they're back. `condition(fn, timeout)` returns false on timeout | [TS timers](https://docs.temporal.io/develop/typescript/timers) |
| Temporal signals/queries | `wf.defineSignal('x')`, `wf.defineQuery<T>('y')`, `wf.setHandler(...)`. Client: `handle.signal(sig, arg)` and `client.workflow.signalWithStart(...)` | [TS message passing](https://docs.temporal.io/develop/typescript/message-passing) |
| Temporal activity retries | Activities retry by default: initial 1 s, backoff 2.0, max interval 100× initial, **unlimited attempts**, no non-retryable errors. "Workflow Executions do not retry by default." **Each retry is NOT written to event history.** You see attempt count and last failure in the UI's *Pending Activities* panel while it retries, then one `ActivityTaskStarted` with `attempt: N` and `lastFailure`. To keep every attempt, log it yourself (Quorum writes each attempt to `plans.events`) | [Retry policies](https://docs.temporal.io/encyclopedia/retry-policies); [Temporal forum](https://community.temporal.io/t/how-to-save-all-retry-attempt-failure-logs/14903) |
| Temporal persistence | `temporal server start-dev --db-filename quorum.db`. "By default, Workflow Executions are lost when the server process dies." UI = `--port` + 1000 = 8233 | [Temporal CLI](https://docs.temporal.io/cli/server) |
| Render Free limits | Spins down after "15 minutes without receiving any inbound traffic". Spin-up "takes about one minute". Ephemeral filesystem. 750 instance-hours/month. No outbound SMTP ports. Only web services, Postgres and Key Value are Free (**no free background workers**). ## 2.3 Architecture, data model, repo layout

### Architecture (text diagram)

```
 ┌────────────── Telegram group (the real friends) ───────────────┐
 │ /join  /me <constraint>  /plan  poll taps  replies w/ photo     │
 └───────▲──────────────────────────────┬──────────────────────────┘
         │ sendMessage/sendPoll         │ getUpdates (long poll, privacy mode ON)
         │ (activities)                 ▼
 ┌───────┴───────────── YOUR LAPTOP (stays awake Sat→Sun) ───────────────────┐
 │  bot.ts ──signal(vote|recap)/start──► Temporal dev server (quorum.db, :8233)│
 │                                          │ tasks                            │
 │                                   worker.ts ── activities: draftPlans,      │
 │                                          │     recheckWeather, storeRecap,  │
 │                                          │     sendPoll, say, savePlan      │
 └──────────────────────────────────────────┼──────────────────────────────────┘
                     HTTPS + shared secret  │  (25 s timeout → retried by Temporal;
                                            ▼   Render cold start = a real flaky call)
 ┌──────────── RENDER FREE WEB SERVICE (sleeps after 15 min) ─────────────┐
 │ Mastra server: agent "quorum" (Gemma 4 via Gemini API)                 │
 │   tools: weather (Open-Meteo), places (Overpass), liveCheck (SerpApi*) │
 │ routes: /quorum/draft  /quorum/recheck  /quorum/remember               │
 │         /p/:planId (public plan page)  /try (judge demo)  /health      │
 └────────────────────────────────────┬────────────────────────────────────┘
                                      ▼
 ┌──────────── MONGODB ATLAS M0 ───────────────────────────────────────────┐
 │ Mastra: threads/messages + vector index (semantic recall, 768-d)        │
 │ App: members · plans · polls · recaps · serp_cache                      │
 └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

For the **post**, redraw it with 5 boxes: Telegram → Laptop (Temporal + worker + bot) → Render (Mastra + Gemma) → Atlas, with Open-Meteo/OSM as a side box. The persuasion rule allows no more than 6 boxes.

**Who owns what (say this in the post):** Temporal owns **time** (waiting, retrying, reminding). Mastra owns **reasoning** (which plan, why). Atlas owns **memory** (who can't do what, what happened last time). Render owns the **public face** (the agent API, the plan page, the judge demo). The laptop holds only the clock and the bot token.

### MongoDB schema (database `quorum`)

```ts
// members: one doc per person who /join'ed. _id = `${chatId}:${userId}`
{ _id, chatId, userId, name, consentAt: Date,
  constraints: [{ text: "knee hates long descents", addedAt: Date }] }
// plans: one doc per workflow. _id = workflowId = `plan-${chatId}-${date}`
{ _id, chatId, date, quorum, status: 'drafting'|'voting'|'locked'|'no-quorum'|'fallback'|'reminded'|'recap'|'done',
  options: [{ title, where, start, durationH, shapedBy: [string], weatherNote }],
  counts: [number], chosen?: {...}, weather?: { checkedAt, maxRain, go },
  events: [{ at: Date, type: string, detail: string }] }   // incl. every activity attempt
// polls: { _id: telegramPollId, planId, messageId }
// recaps: { _id, planId, chatId, userId, name, line, photoFileId?, at }
// serp_cache: { _id: sha1(query), query, results, fetchedAt }   (TTL index 12 h)
// mastra_* collections + vector index: created by @mastra/mongodb (1 of your 3 M0 indexes)
```

Privacy rules (put them in the README): only people who `/join` are stored. `/forget` deletes your member doc. The public plan page shows **first names only, with consent**, or just counts. Photos stay as Telegram `file_id`s and are never re-hosted.

### Hour 0 — Project bootstrap (vibecoding flow): ALWAYS FIRST

This step embeds the standard bootstrap from `vibecoding-bootstrap.md`. Do it **before any feature code**. Order matters, because Entire must be enabled **before** your first agent session so every session is captured.

```bash
mkdir quorum && cd quorum
git init && git config user.name "<YOUR NAME>" && git config user.email "<YOUR EMAIL>"
entire enable -y --agent <claude-code|codex|copilot-cli|cursor|opencode> --checkpoint-backend branch
gh repo create quorum --public --source . --push     # or create on github.com and add the remote
```

`entire enable` makes the first commit if the folder is new, and creates `.entire/settings.json`. When Entire asks to link a commit to the agent session, answer **`a` (always)** ([quickstart](https://docs.entire.io/quickstart.md)).

Then paste this **kickoff prompt** into your coding agent. It is the bootstrap's standard prompt with Quorum-specific rules added:

```
Bootstrap this project for an automated vibecoding flow before any feature code:

   weather re-check, 06:00 reminder, recap); memory in MongoDB Atlas; hosted on Render."
2. Create AGENTS.md with these rules:
   - Read memory.md FIRST every task; UPDATE it LAST (summarize, don't dump — minimize tokens).
   - Edit only relevant files; don't scan the whole repo.
   - For any web UI, use the frontend-design skill.
   - After each working increment, git commit using Conventional Commits

   - QUORUM RULES: never edit src/temporal/workflows.ts after git tag `real-run-start`
     (Temporal determinism) — use wf.patched() or a new workflow type instead.
     Use agent.generate (never stream) with Gemma. Every external call in an activity
     has an explicit AbortSignal.timeout. Never invent place names: only tool output.
     Store only /join'ed members; /forget deletes. No human co-authors in commits.
3. Create .github/copilot-instructions.md pointing to AGENTS.md.
4. Create README.md (stub: what it is + how to run), LICENSE (Apache-2.0), .env.example
   (GOOGLE_API_KEY, MONGODB_URI, MONGODB_DB, TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN, RENDER_URL,

5. Commit: "chore: bootstrap project + agent workflow".

Then stop and show me memory.md and AGENTS.md before building features.
```

After that, every prompt follows the pattern: *"Read memory.md, then <next task>, then update memory.md and commit."*

# Frontend Design

Approach this as the design lead at a design studio known for giving every client a distinct visual identity that is not mistaken for anyone else's. This client has already rejected proposals that felt cliché or templated, and is paying for a distinctive point of view: make deliberate, opinionated choices about palette, typography, and layout that are specific to this brief, and take aesthetic risk if justified.

## Ground your designs in the subject matter

If the brief does not identify what the product or subject matter is, identify it yourself before designing, and confirm with the client. You can come up with one concrete subject, the design's audience, and the design's primary job, as a proposal. If there's any information in your memory about the client's preferences or context about what they're building, use that as a hint. The subject's industry, subject matter, materials, and vernacular are where distinctive visual choices come from — a design for a toy for girls aged 8–11 will be very aesthetically different from a dashboard for financial analysts. Build with the brief's real content and subject matter throughout.

## Design principles

For web designs, the hero is the first thing viewers will see. Open with the most characteristic thing in the subject's world, in the form that is most appropriate: a headline, an image, an animation, a live demo, an interactive moment, or other treatments. Be deliberate with your choice: a big number with a small label, supporting stats, and a gradient accent is the default treatment, so only use it if that's truly the best option.

Typography carries the personality of the page. You don't need a different typeface for display or headline text and body content: use one family or two, and if two, make them clearly distinct.

Choose your typefaces deliberately, not the default families you would reach for on any other project, and set a clear type scale following the default guidance of The Elements of Typographic Style with intentional weights, widths, and spacing. When type is used as a headline or visual element, use the type treatment itself as an active part of the design, not a neutral delivery vehicle for the content.

Default to line lengths of less than 80 characters. Serif typefaces can have slightly longer line lengths; give serif body text slightly more line-height than a sans-serif.

Avoid these default typographic treatments; they are the commonest tells of a generated page:
- Accenting just a single word or phrase in a headline, like putting one word in italic/bold or a different color.
- Using all caps for labels.
- Adding unnecessary typographic labels above content.

Visual structure is information. Structural devices like outlines, borders, numbering, eyebrows, dividers, labels, etc., encode useful information about the content rather than decorate it. Many generic designs use numbered markers (01 / 02 / 03), but that's only appropriate if the content actually is a sequence — like a stepped process or a timeline. Before adding numbered markers, check the content really is a sequence.

Use non-user-triggered motion sparingly and deliberately, only to draw attention. A single orchestrated moment — one page-load sequence or one reveal — lands better than scattered effects; fade-and-slide-up entrances on each section and hover transitions on every card are the generic default and read as AI-generated. Motion that answers a person's action (opening, expanding, confirming) is welcome when it shows what changed.

Consider written content carefully. Often a design brief may not contain real content, and it's up to you to come up with copy and placeholder content. Copy can make a design feel as templated as the design itself. See the below section on writing for more guidance.

## Process: plan, review against the brief, build, critique

For calibration, AI-generated design right now clusters around some traits:
1. a warm cream background (near #F4F1EA) with a high-contrast serif display and a terracotta or warm-clay accent (often near #D97757 — Anthropic's own Claude-interaction accent, so on a user's brief it reads as a tell);
2. a near-black background with a single bright acid-green or vermilion accent;
3. a broadsheet-style layout with hairline rules, zero border-radius, and dense newspaper-like columns;
4. the SaaS-card kit: content chopped into identical rounded cards, one border-radius on everything regardless of hierarchy, the same soft grey shadow (rgba(0,0,0,.1)) under each, and gradient washes as decoration;
5. template chrome that appears whatever the subject: a tracked-out ALL-CAPS eyebrow label above every heading; meta strings joined with middle dots ('A · B · C'); labels built as 'WORD — fragment' with a spaced em dash; tinted near-black (#0B0B0B, #111) standing in for black; a monospace face for small data labels; a '→' appended to link and button text.

All traits are legitimate for some briefs, but they are defaults rather than choices, and they appear regardless of subject. Where the brief pins down a visual direction, follow it exactly — the brief's own words always win, including when it asks for one of these looks. Where it leaves an axis free, don't spend that freedom on one of these defaults. As with a hired human designer, there's often a careful balance between doing what you're good at and taking each project as a chance to experiment and learn.

Work in two passes. First, brainstorm a short design plan based on the client's design brief: create a compact token system with color, type, layout, and principles.
- Color: describe the core base palette as 4–6 named hex values.
- Type: the typefaces and their roles.
- Layout: a layout concept, using one-sentence prose descriptions and ASCII wireframes to ideate and compare. Include alignment guidance; should the content be left aligned, center aligned, justified?
- Principles: the high-level guidance for what makes this page unique.

Then review that plan against the brief before building: if any part of it reads like the generic default you would produce for any similar page (work through a similar prompt to see if you arrive somewhere similar) rather than a choice made for this specific brief — revise that part, say what you changed and why. Only after you've confirmed the relative uniqueness of your design plan should you start to write the code, following the revised plan.

When writing the code, be careful of structuring your CSS selector specificities. It's easy to generate CSS classes that cancel each other out (especially with a type-based selector like .section and an element-based selector like .cta). This can happen often with padding/margin between sections.

## Restraint and self-critique

Spend your boldness in one place. Let one element be the memorable thing, keep everything around it quiet and disciplined, and cut any decoration that does not serve the brief. Build to a quality floor without announcing it: responsive down to mobile, visible keyboard focus, reduced motion respected, visually accessible, harmonious color palettes. Critique your own work as you build, taking screenshots to review if your environment supports it — a picture is worth 1000 tokens. Consider Chanel's advice: before leaving the house, take a look in the mirror and remove one accessory. Human creatives have memory and always try to do something new, so if you have a space to quickly jot down notes about what you've tried, it can help you in future passes.

## More on writing in design

Words appear in a design for one reason: to make it easier to understand and use. They are design content, not decoration. Bring the same intentionality and minimalism to copywriting that you would bring to spacing and color. Before writing anything, ask what the design needs to say, and how it can best be said to help the person navigate the experience.

Write from the end user's perspective. Name things by what users will understand in simple language, not by how the system is built. A user manages notifications, not webhook config. Describe what something is or does in plain terms rather than selling it. Being specific and legible to new users is always better than being clever.

Use active voice as default. A CTA says exactly what happens when it is used: "Save changes," not "Submit." An action keeps the same name through the whole flow, so the button that says "Publish" produces a toast that says "Published." The vocabulary of an interface is the signposting for someone navigating the product. Cohesion and consistency are how people learn their way around.

Treat failure and emptiness as moments for direction, not mood. Explain what went wrong and how to fix it, in the interface's voice rather than a person's. Errors don't apologize, and they are never vague about what happened. An empty screen is an invitation to act.

Keep the tone conversational: plain verbs, sentence case, no filler, with tone matched to the brand and the audience. Let each written element do exactly one job.

lines: +// Offline check of planOuting against the local Temporal dev server: mocked activities, timers in seconds.
+// Covers: happy path (vote → lock → weather ok → reminder → recap → done), no-quorum, rain fallback,
+// a Render call that fails twice before succeeding (retries), and draft failure.
+// Usage: temporal server start-dev (or ./scripts/run-local.sh), then `npx tsx scripts/test-workflow.ts`.
+import { planOuting, vote, recap, type PlanInput } from '../src/temporal/workflows';
+const opt = (title: string, where: string): Option => ({ title, where, start: '07:00', durationH: 2, shapedBy: ['Sara: knee'], weatherNote: 'dry' });
+const OPTIONS = [opt('Walk A', 'Park A'), opt('Walk B', 'Park B'), opt('Walk C', 'Park C')];
+  async draftPlans(p: PlanInput) { if (draftFails) throw new Error('render 502'); log.push(`${p.planId} draft`); return OPTIONS; },
+  async recheckWeather(p: PlanInput, chosen: Option, alts: Option[]) {
+    if (recheckFails > 0) { recheckFails--; log.push(`${p.planId} recheck-fail`); throw new Error('TimeoutError: render asleep'); }
+    return rain ? { go: false, maxRain: 80, fallback: alts[0] } : { go: true, maxRain: 10 };
+  async storeRecap(p: PlanInput, _plan: Option, rs: unknown[]) { log.push(`${p.planId} store ${rs.length}`); },
+  async announce(p: PlanInput, kind: string, data: any) { log.push(`${p.planId} ${kind}${data.plan ? `:${data.plan.where}` : ''}`); },
+  connection: await NativeConnection.connect({ address }), taskQueue: 'quorum-test', activities,
+const client = new Client({ connection: await Connection.connect({ address }) });
+const input = (id: string, quorum = 2): PlanInput => ({ planId: `${id}-${Date.now()}`, chatId: 'test', date: '2026-10-11', quorum,
+  pollCloseAt: s(6), weatherCheckAt: s(8), reminderAt: s(9), outingEndAt: s(10), recapUntil: s(14) });
+const wait = (ms: number) => new Promise((r) => setTimeout(r, ms));
+const check = (name: string, cond: boolean) => { console.log(`${cond ? 'PASS' : 'FAIL'} ${name}`); if (!cond) process.exitCode = 1; };
+  // 1. Happy path, with the weather call failing twice first (initial retry interval 5 s → ~15 s).
+  const ha = await client.workflow.start(planOuting, { taskQueue: 'quorum-test', workflowId: a.planId, args: [a] });
+  await ha.signal(recap, { userId: '1', name: 'Sara', line: 'great view' });
+  await ha.signal(recap, { userId: '2', name: 'Omar', line: 'too early' });
+  check('locked on most-voted option (Park B)', log.includes(`${a.planId} locked:Park B`));
+  check('weather retried twice then succeeded', log.filter((l) => l === `${a.planId} recheck-fail`).length === 2 && log.includes(`${a.planId} recheck`));
+  const hb = await client.workflow.start(planOuting, { taskQueue: 'quorum-test', workflowId: b.planId, args: [b] });
+  check('no-quorum when poll closes short', (await hb.result()) === 'no-quorum');
+  // 3. Rain → fallback plan in the reminder; recap window times out with zero recaps.
+  const hc = await client.workflow.start(planOuting, { taskQueue: 'quorum-test', workflowId: c.planId, args: [c] });
+  check('reminder uses the fallback (Park B)', log.includes(`${c.planId} reminder:Park B`));
+  check('no store when no recaps', !log.some((l) => l.startsWith(`${c.planId} store`)));
+  const hd = await client.workflow.start(planOuting, { taskQueue: 'quorum-test', workflowId: d.planId, args: [{ ...d, pollCloseAt: s(5) }] });

content.text:
# Claude in Chrome browser automation

You have access to browser automation tools (mcp__claude-in-chrome__*) for interacting with web pages in Chrome. Follow these guidelines for effective browser automation.

## Loading deferred tools

If the mcp__claude-in-chrome__* tools are deferred (must be loaded via ToolSearch before use), load every tool you expect to need in ONE ToolSearch call — the select query accepts a comma-separated list — never one call per tool. Start with the core set:

ToolSearch with query "select:mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_context_mcp,mcp__claude-in-chrome__navigate,mcp__claude-in-chrome__computer,mcp__claude-in-chrome__read_page,mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_create_mcp,mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_close_mcp"

Add task-specific tools to the same call when the task obviously needs them: read_console_messages / read_network_requests for debugging, form_input for forms, gif_creator for recordings, javascript_tool for page scripting.

## GIF recording

When performing multi-step browser interactions that the user may want to review or share, use mcp__claude-in-chrome__gif_creator to record them.

You must ALWAYS:
* Capture extra frames before and after taking actions to ensure smooth playback
* Name the file meaningfully to help the user identify it later (e.g., "login_process.gif")

## Console log debugging

You can use mcp__claude-in-chrome__read_console_messages to read console output. Console output may be verbose. If you are looking for specific log entries, use the 'pattern' parameter with a regex-compatible pattern. This filters results efficiently and avoids overwhelming output. For example, use pattern: "[MyApp]" to filter for application-specific logs rather than reading all console output.

## Alerts and dialogs

IMPORTANT: Do not trigger JavaScript alerts, confirms, prompts, or browser modal dialogs through your actions. These browser dialogs block all further browser events and will prevent the extension from receiving any subsequent commands. Instead, when possible, use console.log for debugging and then use the mcp__claude-in-chrome__read_console_messages tool to read those log messages. If a page has dialog-triggering elements:
1. Avoid clicking buttons or links that may trigger alerts (e.g., "Delete" buttons with confirmation dialogs)
2. If you must interact with such elements, warn the user first that this may interrupt the session
3. Use mcp__claude-in-chrome__javascript_tool to check for and dismiss any existing dialogs before proceeding

If you accidentally trigger a dialog and lose responsiveness, inform the user they need to manually dismiss it in the browser.

## Avoid rabbit holes and loops

When using browser automation tools, stay focused on the specific task. If you encounter any of the following, stop and ask the user for guidance:
- Unexpected complexity or tangential browser exploration
- Browser tool calls failing or returning errors after 2-3 attempts
- No response from the browser extension
- Page elements not responding to clicks or input
- Pages not loading or timing out
- Unable to complete the browser task despite multiple approaches

Explain what you attempted, what went wrong, and ask how the user would like to proceed. Do not keep retrying the same failing browser action or explore unrelated pages without checking in first.

## Tab context and session startup

IMPORTANT: At the start of each browser automation session, call mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_context_mcp first to get information about the user's current browser tabs. Use this context to understand what the user might want to work with before creating new tabs.

Never reuse tab IDs from a previous/other session. Follow these guidelines:
1. Only reuse an existing tab if the user explicitly asks to work with it
2. Otherwise, create a new tab with mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_create_mcp
3. If a tool returns an error indicating the tab doesn't exist or is invalid, call tabs_context_mcp to get fresh tab IDs
4. When a tab is closed by the user or a navigation error occurs, call tabs_context_mcp to see what tabs are available

entries.name: mcp__claude-in-chrome__computer
entries.description:
Use a mouse and keyboard to interact with a web browser, and take screenshots. If you don't have a valid tab ID, use tabs_context_mcp first to get available tabs.
* Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element before moving the cursor.
* If you tried clicking on a program or link but it failed to load, even after waiting, try adjusting your click location so that the tip of the cursor visually falls on the element that you want to click.
* Make sure to click any buttons, links, icons, etc with the cursor tip in the center of the element. Don't click boxes on their edges unless asked.

action.description:
The action to perform:
* `left_click`: Click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `right_click`: Click the right mouse button at the specified coordinates to open context menus.
* `double_click`: Double-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `triple_click`: Triple-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `type`: Type a string of text.
* `screenshot`: Take a screenshot of the screen.
* `wait`: Wait for a specified number of seconds.
* `scroll`: Scroll up, down, left, or right at the specified coordinates.
* `key`: Press a specific keyboard key.
* `left_click_drag`: Drag from start_coordinate to coordinate.
* `zoom`: Take a screenshot of a specific region for closer inspection.
* `scroll_to`: Scroll an element into view using its element reference ID from read_page or find tools.
* `hover`: Move the mouse cursor to the specified coordinates or element without clicking. Useful for revealing tooltips, dropdown menus, or triggering hover states.

coordinate.description: (x, y): The x (pixels from the left edge) and y (pixels from the top edge) coordinates. Required for `left_click`, `right_click`, `double_click`, `triple_click`, and `scroll`. For `left_click_drag`, this is the end position.

text.description: The text to type (for `type` action) or the key(s) to press (for `key` action). For `key` action: Provide space-separated keys (e.g., "Backspace Backspace Delete"). Supports keyboard shortcuts using the platform's modifier key (use "cmd" on Mac, "ctrl" on Windows/Linux, e.g., "cmd+a" or "ctrl+a" for select all). Page zoom shortcuts (e.g. "cmd+=", "ctrl+-", "cmd+0") are not supported and will return an error - use the `zoom` action to magnify a region of the page instead.

duration.description: The number of seconds to wait. Required for `wait`. Maximum 10 seconds.

scroll_direction.description: The direction to scroll. Required for `scroll`.

scroll_amount.description: The number of scroll wheel ticks. Optional for `scroll`, defaults to 3.

region.description: (x0, y0, x1, y1): The rectangular region to capture for `zoom`. Coordinates define a rectangle from top-left (x0, y0) to bottom-right (x1, y1) in pixels from the viewport origin. Required for `zoom` action. Useful for inspecting small UI elements like icons, buttons, or text.

scale.description: For `screenshot` and `zoom` only. Scale factor in [0.1, 1] for the returned image; 1 (default) uses the full image token budget, 0.5 returns an image at half the width and height (~quarter of the tokens). # Quorum

A member of your friend group's Telegram chat that turns "we should go out" into an actual outing. A Mastra agent on Gemma 4 drafts plans around everyone's constraints, and a Temporal workflow holds the clock: poll, quorum deadline, weather re-check, morning reminder, recap.

```
Telegram ──► laptop: bot + Temporal dev server + worker ──HTTPS──► Render: Mastra agent (Gemma 4) ──► MongoDB Atlas
                                                                    tools: Open-Meteo, OpenStreetMap
```

- **Temporal** owns time: waiting for votes, the 05:30 weather check, the 06:00 reminder, retrying a sleeping server.
- **Mastra + Gemma 4** own reasoning: which outing, and which constraint shaped it.
- **MongoDB Atlas** owns memory: who joined, their limits, plans, recaps, and semantic recall of past outings.
- **Render** owns the public face: the agent API, the plan page `/p/:id`, and the demo at `/try`.

## Run

Needs Node 22, the [Temporal CLI](https://docs.temporal.io/cli), a Google AI Studio key, an Atlas M0 cluster and a Telegram bot token.

```bash
npm install
cp .env.example .env            # fill in keys
npm run smoke -- --n 6          # Gemma tool-call check (full Gate 1: npm run smoke)
npm run places                  # cache real spots around HOME_LAT/HOME_LON
npm run dev                     # Mastra server on :4111 (or deploy to Render, below)
```

Laptop side (separate terminals):

```bash
./scripts/run-local.sh          # Temporal dev server, UI on :8233
npm run worker
npm run bot
```

content.text:
All the code from Part II of the playbook is written and committed in 6 commits on `main`. Nothing is pushed yet. None of it has run against real Gemma, Atlas or Telegram yet, because there's no `.env`.

**What I checked:**
- The project typechecks cleanly. `mastra build` and `mastra dev` both serve `/`, `/try`, `/p/:id` and `/health`.
- `npm run test:workflow` runs the real workflow on the local Temporal server with mocked activities and compressed timers. All 9 checks pass: lock on the most-voted option, two failed weather calls then a retry that succeeds, no-quorum, rain fallback, and "Can't make it" never counting as a yes.
- The Temporal worker bundles under ESM, so the CommonJS fallback isn't needed.
- I reviewed the plan page and `/try` in your browser with fake data and fixed a timeline bug I found.

**Changes from the spec skeleton:**
- **Overpass was down everywhere I tried today.** Place lookup now tries mirrors, then Photon (also OSM data, but weaker names), and caches results in Atlas. Run `npm run places` once Overpass is up so drafts never wait on it.
- **Invented places are dropped.** Every draft checks Gemma's place names against the real place list and drops invented ones. If fewer than 2 real options are left, code builds them from real places.
- **Drafts get longer timeouts** (90 s for the request, 150 s for the activity). A Gemma draft with tools can take longer than 25 s. The weather re-check keeps a short 30 s timeout so Render's cold start still shows up as a retry.
- **The workflow carries on when retries run out.** If drafting fails, it tells the group. If the weather check fails, it keeps the plan and says the forecast is unknown.
- **The public plan page shows only vote counts by default.** Names appear only with `PUBLIC_NAMES=on`.

I didn't use your browser to create accounts or API keys. I'm not allowed to create accounts, and making keys or tokens changes your account settings, which needs your yes for each one.

**What you need to do:**
1. **Get keys:** a Google AI Studio API key, an Atlas M0 cluster (Network Access `0.0.0.0/0`), a Telegram bot from @BotFather (leave privacy mode on and don't make it an admin), and a Render account.
2. **Fill in `.env`:** `cp .env.example .env`, then add the keys, `HOME_LAT`, `HOME_LON` and `QUORUM_SHARED_SECRET` (make one with `openssl rand -hex 24`).
3. **Run Gate 1:** `npm run smoke` (20 drafts). If fewer than 16 pass, set `TOOL_MODE=prefetch` in `.env` and on Render.
4. **Cache places:** `npm run places`.
5. **Push and deploy:** `git push`, then on Render choose New → Blueprint → this repo and set the secret env vars. Put the `onrender.com` URL in `.env` as both `RENDER_URL` and `PUBLIC_URL`, and check that `/health` returns 200.
6. **Start the laptop side:** the Temporal dev server is already running in the background from my tests (UI on :8233); after a reboot, start it with `./scripts/run-local.sh`. Then run `npm run worker` and `npm run bot`.
7. **Test in a group:** `/join`, `/me no car`, then `/plan test`. That's a full run in about 10 minutes.
8. **Before the real run:** `git tag real-run-start && git push --tags`, then `/plan 2026-10-11 4`. Don't edit `src/temporal/workflows.ts` after the tag.

If you add the Google key to `.env` and tell me, I'll run Gate 1 and fix whatever it shows.

The bot now runs on Discord instead of Telegram. It's committed (`f5abefa`) and nothing is pushed yet. The typecheck is clean and the workflow test still passes 9/9. With a fake token the bot gets as far as Discord rejecting the login, which is as far as I can test without a real token.

**How it works on Discord:**
- **Commands:** `/join`, `/me limit:…`, `/mine`, `/forget`, `/plan date:2026-10-11 people:4` (or `date:test`), `/status`, `/cancel`, `/recap line:… photo:…`, `/help`.
- **Poll:** a multi-select menu under the options message: pick every option you can make, or "Can't make it". The vote count on the message updates live, and each voter gets a private "Got it, you picked: …". I didn't use Discord's native polls because they cut answers off at 55 characters.
- **Recap:** the recap message has an **Add my recap** button that opens a text box, or people use `/recap` to attach a photo.
- **Privacy:** the bot asks for no privileged access, so it never sees normal messages, only slash commands and taps on its own buttons. That's Discord's version of Telegram's privacy mode.
- **One channel per group:** the roster and plans belong to the channel where people `/join`.
- **Optional ping:** set `DISCORD_PING_ROLE` and the 06:00 reminder pings that role.

**Bug fixed along the way:** the old bot would have refused every `/plan test`. Its "poll closes too soon" check required at least 10 minutes, but a test poll closes after 3. The limit is now 2 minutes.

entries.name: Monitor
entries.description:
Start a background monitor that streams events from a long-running script. Each stdout line is an event — you keep working and notifications arrive in the chat. Events arrive on their own schedule and are not replies from the user, even if one lands while you're waiting for the user to answer a question.

Pick by how many notifications you need:
- **One** ("tell me when the server is ready / the build finishes") → use **Bash with `run_in_background`** and a command that exits when the condition is true, e.g. `until grep -q "Ready in" dev.log; do sleep 0.5; done`. You get a single completion notification when it exits.
- **One per occurrence, until the monitor expires (re-arm to continue)** ("tell me every time an ERROR line appears") → Monitor with an unbounded command (`tail -f`, `inotifywait -m`, `while true`).
- **One per occurrence, until a known end** ("emit each CI step result, stop when the run completes") → Monitor with a command that emits lines and then exits.

Your script's stdout is the event stream. Each line becomes a notification. Exit ends the watch.

  # Each matching log line is an event
  tail -f /var/log/app.log | grep --line-buffered "ERROR"

  # Each file change is an event
  inotifywait -m --format '%e %f' /watched/dir

  # Poll GitHub for new PR comments and emit one line per new comment
  last=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)
  while true; do
    now=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)
    gh api "repos/owner/repo/issues/123/comments?since=$last" --jq '.[] | "\(.user.login): \(.body)"'
    last=$now; sleep 30
  done

  # Node script that emits events as they arrive (e.g. WebSocket listener)
  node watch-for-events.js

  # Per-occurrence with a natural end: emit each CI check as it lands, exit when the run completes
  prev=""
  while true; do
    s=$(gh pr checks 123 --json name,bucket)
    cur=$(jq -r '.[] | select(.bucket!="pending") | "\(.name): \(.bucket)"' <<<"$s" | sort)
    comm -13 <(echo "$prev") <(echo "$cur")
    prev=$cur
    jq -e 'all(.bucket!="pending")' <<<"$s" >/dev/null && break
    sleep 30
  done

**Don't use an unbounded command for a single notification.** `tail -f`, `inotifywait -m`, and `while true` never exit on their own, so the monitor stays armed until timeout even after the event has fired. For "tell me when X is ready," use Bash `run_in_background` with an `until` loop instead (one notification, ends in seconds). Note that `tail -f log | grep -m 1 ...` does *not* fix this: if the log goes quiet after the match, `tail` never receives SIGPIPE and the pipeline hangs anyway.

**Script quality:**
- Every pipe stage must flush per line or matches sit in its buffer unseen: `grep` needs `--line-buffered`, `awk` needs `fflush()`. `head` cannot flush at all — `| head -N` delivers nothing until N matches accumulate, then ends the stream.
- In poll loops, handle transient failures (`curl ... || true`) — one failed request shouldn't kill the monitor.
- Poll intervals: 30s+ for remote APIs (rate limits), 0.5-1s for local checks.
- Write a specific `description` — it appears in every notification ("errors in deploy.log" not "watching logs").
- Only stdout is the event stream. Stderr goes to the output file (readable via Read) but does not trigger notifications — for a command you run directly (e.g. `python train.py 2>&1 | grep --line-buffered ...`), merge stderr with `2>&1` so its failures reach your filter. (No effect on `tail -f` of an existing log — that file only contains what its writer redirected.)

**Coverage — silence is not success.** When watching a job or process for an outcome, your filter must match every terminal state, not just the happy path. A monitor that greps only for the success marker stays silent through a crashloop, a hung process, or an unexpected exit — and silence looks identical to "still running." Before arming, ask: *if this process crashed right now, would my filter emit anything?* If not, widen it.

  # Wrong — silent on crash, hang, or any non-success exit
  tail -f run.log | grep --line-buffered "elapsed_steps="

  # Right — one alternation covering progress + the failure signatures you'd act on
  tail -f run.log | grep -E --line-buffered "elapsed_steps=|Traceback|Error|FAILED|assert|Killed|OOM"

For poll loops checking job state, emit on every terminal status (`succeeded|failed|cancelled|timeout`), not just success. If you cannot confidently enumerate the failure signatures, broaden the grep alternation rather than narrow it — some extra noise is better than missing a crashloop.

**Output volume**: Every stdout line is a conversation message, so the filter should be selective — but selective means "the lines you'd act on," not "only good news." Never pipe raw logs; filter to exactly the success and failure signals you care about. Monitors that produce too many events are automatically stopped; restart with a tighter filter if this happens.

Stdout lines within 200ms are batched into a single notification, so multiline output from a single event groups naturally.

The script runs in the same shell environment as Bash. Exit ends the watch (exit code is reported). Every monitor expires after `timeout_ms` (default 5 minutes, at most 30 minutes): it is killed and you get one notice with the event count. Re-arm it if you still need the watch; for a long watch (PR monitoring, log tails) set `timeout_ms` to the maximum and re-arm on each expiry, and widen the filter if an expiry with no events was unexpected. Use TaskStop to cancel early.
**ws source** — open a WebSocket and stream each incoming text frame as an event. No shell, no polling: the server pushes, you get notified.

  Monitor({
    ws: {url: 'wss://events.example.com/stream', protocols: ['v1']},
    description: 'deploy events',
  })

Each text frame becomes one notification (multiline frames stay as one event). Binary frames are reported as `[binary frame, N bytes]` rather than passed through. Socket close ends the watch with the close code surfaced; errors are surfaced before close. Same rate limiting as bash — a firehose will be suppressed and eventually stopped, so subscribe to a filtered feed where one exists.

Prefer this over `command: 'websocat wss://…'` — it avoids the extra process and line-buffering pitfalls. Use bash when you need to transform or filter frames with shell tools before they become events.

When an event lands that the user would want to act on now — an error appeared, the status they were waiting on flipped — send a PushNotification. Not every event is worth a push; the ones that change what they'd do next are.

description.description: Short human-readable description of what you are monitoring (shown in notifications).

timeout_ms.description: Kill the monitor after this deadline. Default 300000ms. Deadlines above 1800000ms are capped to 1800000ms. You are notified at expiry and can re-arm.

command.description: Shell command or script. Each stdout line is an event; exit ends the watch.

ws.description: WebSocket to open. Each text frame is an event; binary frames are reported as a placeholder line. Socket close ends the watch. Cannot be combined with command.

One real draft for Islamabad went through the same route Temporal calls, and it worked in 83 s: 2 tool calls, 2 options at real places (Kachnar Park, F-11/2 Park), each listing the roster limits that shaped it, 0 invented places, no fallback.

**Done since you added the keys:**
- **Atlas:** the login was failing because the password in `MONGODB_URI` still had the `< >` from Atlas's template. I removed them; your original `.env` is backed up in my scratchpad. Atlas now connects, and the vector index for semantic recall is ready.
- **Gate 1 passed.** Results are saved in `docs/evidence/gemma-smoke.md` for the write-up:

| Model | Valid with tool calls | Invented places | Median time | API errors retried |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Gemma 4 26B | 8/8 | 0 | 128 s | 0 |
| Gemma 4 31B | 7/8 | 0 | 202 s | 4 |

  I made 26B the default, with tools called by Gemma itself (`TOOL_MODE=native`). Having code fetch the tools instead wasn't faster (120–193 s), so the time is in Gemma itself.
- **Timeouts:** drafts take minutes on the free tier, so draft and recap calls now wait up to 5 minutes. The original 90 s would have killed every real draft.
- **Places:** Overpass was down all day. Place lookup now falls back to Nominatim, which finds Margalla Hills National Park, Shakarparian and Rawal Lake Viewpoint. Results are cached in Atlas.
- **Discord:** with your OK I authorized the bot into your "quorum" server. It's online as `quorum#1044` with its slash commands.
- **Code:** everything is pushed to GitHub, and the workflow test still passes 9/9.

**Running right now, in my session:** the Temporal server, the worker, the bot, and the agent server on `localhost:4111`. The agent server stands in for Render until it's deployed, which also means `/p/` links in Discord only open on this laptop for now. These stop when this session ends, so for the weekend run them in your own terminals.

**What only you can do:**
1. **Test in Discord now:** run `/join`, `/me limit:no car`, then `/plan date:test people:1`. Options take about 2 minutes, then the poll appears; pick one, and the reminder and recap steps follow over the next ~8 minutes. I didn't type these myself because that would be sending messages as you.
2. **Render:** log in at dashboard.render.com, then New → Blueprint → `ArqamWaheed/quorum`. When it asks for secrets, paste `GOOGLE_API_KEY`, `MONGODB_URI` and `QUORUM_SHARED_SECRET` from your `.env`. I'm not allowed to type keys into web forms. Once `https://<name>.onrender.com/health` returns 200, tell me and I'll switch `RENDER_URL` and `PUBLIC_URL` over and check the deploy.
3. **Before the real run:** `git tag real-run-start && git push --tags`, then `/plan date:2026-10-11 people:4`.

closers, staged openers, forced triads, dashes everywhere, inflated claims, sales

- hyperframes-core: The HyperFrames composition contract — build one renderable project. content.text:
Quorum works end to end in your Discord channel. I ran two compressed test runs and then started the real plan for Sat Oct 17.

**Test run 1, the normal path:** the bot drafted 3 options in about 72 seconds. I voted for option 1 and the plan locked. The weather check found 12% rain, so it stayed on the plan. Then came the reminder, the recap request, my one-line test recap, and "Saved 1 recap".

**Test run 2, the failure cases:**
- **Crash:** I killed the worker with `kill -9` and restarted the Temporal server while the poll was open. The workflow came back where it was, my vote still landed, and the plan locked.
- **Server asleep:** I stopped the agent server just before the weather check, standing in for Render's cold start. Temporal logged four failed attempts (`ECONNREFUSED`) and succeeded on the fifth after I restarted it.
- **Rain:** with the rain limit set to 0%, the reminder switched to the backup, "Visit Childrens Park".
- **No recap:** when nobody sent one, the bot posted "No recaps came in" and closed the plan.

**Fixed along the way:**
- **Test poll too short:** the first test run you started yourself closed before you could vote, because drafting alone takes about 2 minutes. Test polls now stay open 7 minutes.
- **Wrong times in the lock message:** it always said 05:30 and 06:00, even in test runs. It now shows the actual check times.
- **Small fixes:** "needs 1 people" now reads "1 person", the rain line is clearer when the plan switches, and the weather-check timeout went from 30 s to 45 s, which still leaves room for Render's cold-start retries.

Screenshots of the plan page, the Temporal timeline and the retry panel are in `docs/evidence/`. Everything is committed and pushed, tagged `real-run-start`, so the workflow code is frozen. I set the quorum to 1 because you're the only person who has joined. I deleted nothing, so your `/join` and limits are still there.

**The real plan is waiting for a vote.** The options are posted in #general: Kachnar Park, Childrens Park and CDA Park. The poll closes **Fri Oct 16 at 22:00**, then the weather check runs Sat at 05:30 and the reminder at 06:00. I didn't vote for you, because this one is a real outing. Use the menu under the options message before Friday night.

**For the real run to work:**
- **Keep the laptop on and awake until Saturday's recap**, with all four processes running: the Temporal server, the worker, the agent server and the bot. They're running inside this Claude session now, so if it closes they stop. You'd then restart them in your own terminals (`./scripts/run-local.sh`, `npm run dev`, `npm run worker`, `npm run bot`). The plan itself survives a restart, as test run 2 showed.
- **Render is still not deployed.** That needs you to log in and paste the three secrets into Render's form. Until then the plan page links only open on this laptop, and the cold start was simulated rather than real.

957	# PART IV — WRITING PHASE: THE FULL DRAFT POST
958	
959	Below is a template-compliant draft. **It is scaffolding. Rewrite every sentence in your own voice.** Keep the structure: the minutes opening, the template sections in order, and the tables. Replace every `{{…}}` with real data, or delete the sentence. Delete every `<!-- note -->` before publishing.
960	
961	~~~~markdown
962	---
963	title: "Motion carried, {{YES_COUNT}}–{{NO_COUNT}}: the weekend our group chat stopped saying 'we should'"
964	published: false
965	description: "Group plans don't die from disagreement. They die because nobody holds the clock. Quorum is a Gemma 4 agent in our group chat, with a Temporal workflow holding the clock."
966	tags: devchallenge, hf26challenge, showdev, typescript
967	cover_image: {{COVER_IMAGE_URL}}
968	---
969	
970	*This is a submission for the [Hacktoberfest Open-Source AI Challenge Week 1: Touch Grass](https://dev.to/challenges/hacktoberfest-week1-2026-10-05)*
971	
972	> **Minutes: {{GROUP_NAME}}, Saturday {{SAT_DATE}}**
973	> **Present:** {{GROUP_SIZE}} humans, one agent.
974	> **Item 1, the record.** Since {{SINCE_DATE}}, this chat has said "we should go out" {{WE_SHOULD_COUNT}} times. Outings that followed: {{OUTINGS_COUNT}}.
975	> **Item 2, the motion.** {{PLAN_TITLE}}, Sunday at {{START_TIME}}. Proposed by the agent; shaped by "{{SHAPED_BY_EXAMPLE}}".
976	> **Item 3, the vote.** {{YES_COUNT}} yes, {{NO_COUNT}} can't make it. Quorum of {{QUORUM}} reached at {{QUORUM_TIME}}.
977	> **Resolved:** we go.
978	
979	You know how this goes. Someone says "we should do something this weekend." Three thumbs-up. A poll appears, and nobody closes it. Friday night nobody has sent the reminder. On Sunday it's raining, or it isn't, but either way nobody is outside.
980	
981	**Group plans don't die from disagreement. They die because nobody holds the clock.**
982	
983	<!-- note: 2–3 lines max. Only real past attempts. -->
984	Our group has tried the usual fixes:
985	
986	| What we tried | How it died |
987	|---|---|
988	| The chat's own poll | {{WHY_POLL_DIED}} |
989	| One of us organising | {{WHY_ORGANISER_DIED}} |
990	| A shared calendar invite | {{WHY_CALENDAR_DIED}} |
991	
992	So this weekend we added one more member to the chat. It's called Quorum, and its only job is to hold the clock.
993	
994	{% youtube {{YOUTUBE_ID}} %}
995	
996	**Live demo:** {{RENDER_URL}} *(free Render instance; the first load can take about a minute while it wakes, which turns out to matter below)*
997	**Repo:** https://github.com/{{GITHUB_USER}}/quorum *(Apache-2.0)*
998	
999	## What I Built
1000	
1001	Quorum lives in a Telegram group. You never open an app. For each friend, the whole interaction is:
1002	
1003	1. **`/join`**, then one line about yourself: `/me knee hates long descents`, `/me no car`, `/me home by 11`.
1004	2. Someone types **`/plan 2026-10-11 4`** (the date and how many yeses make it real). Quorum replies with 2–3 real places nearby. Each one says which of your constraints shaped it:
1005	   > {{REAL_OPTION_SCREENSHOT_OR_TEXT}}
1006	3. A **poll**. You tap what you can make. When {{QUORUM}} people can make the same option, it locks. If the deadline ({{POLL_CLOSE_LOCAL}} the night before) passes first, Quorum says so and nobody feels guilty.
1007	4. At **05:30** it re-checks the rain for the exact hours you'll be out. At **06:00** it sends the reminder (or the rain-proof alternative). After you're back, it asks for one photo and one line, and remembers them for next time.
1008	
1009	Across the whole weekend, the median friend touched Quorum **{{TAPS_PER_PERSON}} times**. Everything else happened outside.
1010	
1011	**Who it's for:** any group of 4–8 people who keep saying "we should". It suits the friend who always ends up organising, and would like not to.
1012	
1013	> **What's real and what isn't**
1014	> - Real: {{GROUP_SIZE}} friends (first names used with permission), the chat messages, the Temporal event history, the timings, the photos.
1015	> - Real but small: one weekend. That is a story, not a study.
1016	> - Not live after publishing: the Telegram bot and the Temporal worker ran on my laptop for the weekend. The Render page, the plan page and `/try` stay up.
1017	
1018	## Demo
1019	
1020	**Try it without joining any chat:** {{RENDER_URL}}/try. Enter 3–5 made-up people, each with one constraint, plus a city and a date. You'll get 2–3 options, each listing which constraint shaped it. It's rate-limited to protect the free Gemma quota.
1021	
1022	**The real run** has its own public plan page: {{RENDER_URL}}/p/{{PLAN_ID}}. It shows the status timeline and every retry.
1023	
1024	### Sunday, {{SUN_DATE}}: what actually happened
1025	
1026	| Time (local) | What happened |
1027	|---|---|
1028	| Sat {{START_LOCAL}} | `/plan`: {{OPTION_COUNT}} options proposed in {{DRAFT_SECONDS}} s |
1029	| Sat {{QUORUM_TIME}} | Quorum reached: {{YES_COUNT}} of {{GROUP_SIZE}} |
1030	| Sun 05:30 | Weather re-check. Render had been asleep for {{IDLE_HOURS}} h, and the call succeeded on attempt **{{COLD_START_ATTEMPTS}}** after **{{COLD_START_SECONDS}} s** |
1031	| Sun 06:00 | Reminder sent: "{{REMINDER_TEXT}}" |
1032	| Sun {{DEPART_TIME}}–{{RETURN_TIME}} | {{CAME_COUNT}} of us at {{PLACE}} |
1033	
1034	![{{ALT_TEXT_GROUP_PHOTO}}]({{GROUP_PHOTO_URL}})
1035	
1036	> "{{WHAT_THEY_SAID_1}}" ({{FRIEND_1_FIRST_NAME}})
1037	> "{{WHAT_THEY_SAID_2}}" ({{FRIEND_2_FIRST_NAME}})
1038	
1039	**What it got wrong:** {{AGENT_MISTAKE}}. **What I changed:** {{FIX}}.
1040	
1041	## Code
1042	
1043	{% github {{GITHUB_USER}}/quorum %}
1044	
1045	Where to look:
1046	- `src/temporal/workflows.ts`: the whole weekend as one function (about 40 lines)
1047	- `src/temporal/activities.ts`: Render/Gemma calls with retry, and Telegram calls
1048	- `src/mastra/agents/quorum.ts`: the agent, its tools and its memory
1049	- `src/bot/telegram.ts`: chat commands, plus poll votes turned into workflow signals
1050	- `render.yaml`: one free web service
1051	
1052	The heart of it is a vote that can wait for hours and survive restarts:
1053	
1054	```ts
1055	const reached = await wf.condition(
1056	  () => tally(votes, options.length).count >= p.quorum,   // enough people for one option…
1057	  until(p.pollCloseAt),                                   // …or the deadline, whichever first
1058	);
1059	```
1060

title: "Nobody holds the clock: a Discord member that keeps time until your friends are actually outside"
published: false
description: "Group plans don't die from disagreement. They die because nobody holds the clock. Quorum is a Gemma 4 agent in a Discord channel, with a Temporal workflow holding the clock."
tags: devchallenge, hf26challenge, showdev, typescript
cover_image: <COVER_IMAGE_URL or delete this line>
---

*This is a submission for the [Hacktoberfest Open-Source AI Challenge Week 1: Touch Grass](https://dev.to/challenges/hacktoberfest-week1-2026-10-05)*

> **Minutes: #general, Sunday 11 October 2026, 15:27–15:40**
> **Present:** one human, one agent.
> **Item 1, the motion.** Morning stroll at Kachnar Park, 08:00, about 2 hours. Proposed by the agent; shaped by "no car" and "home by 11".
> **Item 2, the vote.** 1 yes. Quorum of 1 reached at 15:29.
> **Item 3, the weather.** Re-checked at the scheduled time: up to 12% rain. Plan stands.
> **Resolved:** reminder sent, recap filed, plan closed. Total time: 13 minutes, because this was the compressed rehearsal.

You know how this goes. Someone says "we should do something this weekend." Three thumbs-up. A poll appears and nobody closes it. Friday night nobody sends the reminder. On Sunday it's raining, or it isn't, and either way nobody is outside.

**Group plans don't die from disagreement. They die because nobody holds the clock.**

So I built one more member for the chat. It's called Quorum, and its only job is to hold the clock.

{% youtube <YOUTUBE_ID> %}

**Live demo:** <RENDER_URL> *(free Render instance: the first load can take about a minute while it wakes, which matters below)*
**Repo:** https://github.com/ArqamWaheed/quorum *(Apache-2.0)*

## What I Built

Quorum lives in a Discord channel. You never open an app. The whole interaction is:

1. **`/join`**, then one line about what limits you: `/me no car`, `/me home by 11`, `/me knee hates long descents`.
2. Someone runs **`/plan date:2026-10-17 people:4`** (the date, and how many yeses make it real). Quorum replies with 2–3 real places near home. Each one lists the limits that shaped it:
   > **1. Morning stroll at Kachnar Park**
   > Kachnar Park, 08:00 for 2 h. Light rain probability is low (10%).
   > Shaped by: GammaUwU: no car; GammaUwU: home by 11
3. A **poll**: a menu where you pick every option you can make. When enough people can make the same option, it locks. If the deadline (22:00 the night before) passes first, Quorum says so and nobody feels guilty.
4. At **05:30** it re-checks the rain for the exact hours you'll be out. At **06:00** it sends the reminder, or the rain-proof alternative. When you're back, it asks for one line (and a photo if you like) and remembers it for next time.

**Who it's for:** any group of 4–8 people who keep saying "we should", and especially the friend who always ends up organising and would rather not.

> **What's real and what isn't**
> - Real: every run below happened on my machine against the live services (Gemma 4 on the Gemini API, MongoDB Atlas, Discord, Open-Meteo, OpenStreetMap). The timings and logs are copied from the plan's event log.
> - Not real yet: a group outing. I built this in a weekend and the friends' Saturday is after the deadline. So what you'll see is a solo end-to-end run plus deliberate failure drills. A real plan for 17 October is open in the channel right now.
> - Not live after publishing: the Discord bot and the Temporal worker run on my laptop. The Render page, `/try` and the plan pages stay up.
> - Why Discord: I started on Telegram, but Telegram is blocked in Pakistan, where I live. Swapping the chat adapter took one file. Nothing else changed.

## Demo

**Try it without joining any chat:** <RENDER_URL>/try. Enter a few made-up people, each with a limit, plus a city and a date. You get 2–3 options, each listing which limit shaped it. It's rate-limited to protect the free Gemma quota.

### The rehearsal, minute by minute

`/plan date:test` runs the identical workflow with every timer compressed into minutes:

| Time | What happened |
|---|---|
| 15:27:19 | `/plan date:test people:1` |
| 15:28:31 | 3 options posted (Gemma 4 + tools: 72 s) |
| 15:29:09 | Vote landed, quorum reached, plan **locked** |
| 15:36:18 | Weather re-check: max 12% rain in the window, keep the plan |
| 15:37:18 | "Good morning" reminder |
| 15:39:18 | Recap requested |
| 15:40:19 | Recap stored in Atlas and agent memory (16 s); plan **done** |

### The failure drills

Then I ran it again and tried to break it.

| Drill | What I did | What happened |
|---|---|---|
| Crash mid-poll | `kill -9` the worker, then stopped and restarted the Temporal server | The workflow came back in `voting`. My vote landed and the plan locked |
| Agent server asleep | Stopped the agent server right before the weather check | 4 failed attempts (`ECONNREFUSED`), then success on attempt 5 when it came back. Every attempt is on the plan page |
| Rain | Restarted the agent server with a 0% rain limit | The reminder switched: "Rain is likely on the original plan, so we're switching to: Visit Childrens Park" |
| Nobody writes a recap | Ignored the recap request | After the window: "No recaps came in. I've closed this plan." |

**What it got wrong:** in my first test the poll closed **53 seconds** after the options appeared. The test schedule gave voting 3 minutes from `/plan`, and drafting alone took 2 minutes on the free tier. **What I changed:** the test poll now stays open 7 minutes. In real runs the poll is open for days, so it never mattered there, but a demo that closes before you can vote is a bug.

## Code

{% github ArqamWaheed/quorum %}

Where to look:
- `src/temporal/workflows.ts`: the whole outing as one function
- `src/temporal/activities.ts`: calls to the agent server with retries, and Discord messages
- `src/mastra/agents/quorum.ts`: the agent, its tools and its memory
- `src/bot/discord.ts`: slash commands, plus votes turned into workflow signals
- `render.yaml`: one free web service

The heart of it is a vote that can wait for days and survive restarts:

```ts
const reached = await wf.condition(
  () => tally(votes, options.length).count >= p.quorum, // enough people for one option…
  until(p.pollCloseAt),                                 // …or the deadline, whichever first
);
```

## How I Built It

```
Discord ──► laptop: Temporal dev server + worker + bot ──► Render: Mastra agent (Gemma 4)
                                                               │      └── Open-Meteo, OpenStreetMap
                                                               ▼
                                                       MongoDB Atlas (memory)
```

**Four owners, one job each.** Temporal owns *time*. Mastra owns *reasoning*. Atlas owns *memory*. Render owns the *public face*.

**1. Temporal holds the clock, not cron or `setTimeout`.**
The outing is one workflow. Votes arrive as signals, `condition()` waits for quorum or the deadline, and `sleep()` waits until 05:30 and 06:00. Temporal persists those timers, which the crash drill proves: after `kill -9` and a server restart, the workflow picked up where it was. The bot does all the time math and hands the workflow absolute timestamps, which keeps it deterministic. I froze `workflows.ts` with a git tag before starting the real plan, because Temporal replays history against the code.
*Concession:* the Temporal server is the open-source dev server on my laptop (`temporal server start-dev --db-filename quorum.db`). Temporal Cloud asks for a card. If the laptop sleeps, the reminder is late, not lost.

**2. A sleeping server is a test, not a bug.**
The agent runs on Render's free tier, which sleeps after 15 idle minutes and takes about a minute to wake. The weather check has a 45-second timeout and a retry policy (5 s initial, ×2 backoff, 12 attempts), so a cold start shows up as failed attempts followed by a success. Here's the drill, copied from the plan's event log:

| Attempt | Result |
|---|---|
| 1 | failed after 4 ms: fetch failed (`ECONNREFUSED`) |
| 2 | failed after 2 ms |
| 3 | failed after 2 ms |
| 4 | failed after 5 ms |
| 5 | ok in 25.9 s |

Temporal doesn't write each retry into the event history; it keeps the attempt count and the last failure. So every attempt is also logged to the plan's own event list, which is what the plan page shows.

**3. Mastra reasons, and only reasons.**
The agent has two tools, `weather` (Open-Meteo) and `places` (OpenStreetMap), plus memory, and returns structured options. Its instructions forbid any place name that didn't come from the places tool. The code checks anyway: an option whose place isn't in the tool's list is dropped, and if fewer than 2 survive, code builds them from real places. Across 16 smoke-test drafts, it dropped **0** invented places.
*Failure I hit:* the public Overpass servers were down all weekend (504s and timeouts on every mirror). *Fix:* places fall back to Nominatim (the same OpenStreetMap data, ranked by importance), and results are cached in Atlas. Around Islamabad that gives Margalla Hills National Park, Shakarparian and Rawal Lake Viewpoint.
*Why not let the agent run the schedule too?* An LLM loop can't sleep for 7 hours and wake up on time. A workflow can't decide that a long descent is bad for a knee. Each does the part it's good at.

**4. Gemma 4, measured rather than assumed.**
Gemma 4 has built-in function calling, but Mastra's model catalogue doesn't mark the Gemma 4 IDs as tool-capable. So I ran the same planning prompt with a fake 5-person roster, 8 times per model, before trusting it:

| Model (same agent code, Gemini API free tier) | Valid plans with tool calls | Invented places | Median time | API errors retried |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `gemma-4-26b-a4b-it` | 8/8 | 0 | 128 s | 0 |
| `gemma-4-31b-it` | 7/8 | 0 | 202 s | 4 |

26B runs Quorum. *Failure I hit:* 31B returned "Internal error encountered" on about half the calls at first. *Fix:* transient Gemini errors are retried inside the draft call and then by Temporal. The remaining cost is latency: about 2 minutes per draft on the free tier. Having code fetch the tools instead of Gemma made no difference (120–193 s), so the time goes into generation, and every timeout is sized for it.

**5. Atlas remembers what a context window forgets.**
The roster (`/me` lines) is a plain collection, so it never depends on the model deciding to call a "remember" tool. Everything said to the agent also goes into Mastra memory on Atlas, with semantic recall over **Atlas Vector Search** (Gemini embeddings, 3072 dimensions, cosine), scoped to the whole channel. Recaps go there too, so next week's draft can see how last week went.
*Concession:* the free M0 cluster allows 3 search/vector indexes in total. Mastra uses two.

**What works and what doesn't:**

| Capability | Status |
|---|---|
| Poll → quorum → weather re-check → reminder → recap, end to end | ✓ (compressed rehearsal) |
| Crash-resume (`kill -9` worker + server restart) | ✓ |
| Sleeping-server retries absorbed | ✓ (drill on the laptop; <RENDER: real cold start or delete> ) |
| Rain fallback | ✓ (forced) |
| Native Gemma tool calls in Mastra | ✓ |
| Semantic recall index on Atlas Vector Search | ✓ index ready; no week-two recall yet |
| A real group outing | ✗ not before the deadline; plan for 17 Oct is open |
| Fully local mode (Ollama) | ✗ wired up, not measured |

## Why Does Open Innovation Matter?

A group chat holds things people wouldn't put in an app: whose knee is bad, who's broke this month, whose parents set a curfew. That shaped three choices.

- **Open weights mean a local option exists.** The same agent switches to `gemma4:e4b` on Ollama with one environment variable (`QUORUM_MODEL=ollama:gemma4:e4b`). I haven't benchmarked it yet, but the switch is there, and nothing would leave the machine. A closed API offers no such switch.
- **Honest trade-off:** the runs above used Gemma 4 through the Gemini API's free tier, which says content may be used to improve Google's products. The bot says so in `/help`, and it only ever sees slash commands and taps on its own buttons, never ordinary chat messages.
- **Open infrastructure all the way down.** Temporal's open-source server made a durable, multi-day workflow possible at $0 on a laptop. Mastra is Apache-2.0. The places come from OpenStreetMap and the forecasts from Open-Meteo. Total bill: **$0**.

## My Agent Session

I built Quorum with Claude Code, with the [Entire CLI](https://docs.entire.io) capturing every session and linking it to the commit it produced. For example, the checkpoint behind the fix for the 53-second poll:

> ● Checkpoint 199ef0496889
> commits 68e95ec fix: longer test-run poll window; drafting alone takes ~2 min on the free tier

All checkpoints: https://github.com/ArqamWaheed/quorum/tree/entire/checkpoints/v1

## Prize Categories

- **Best Use of Temporal**: the whole outing is one workflow (`planOuting`): vote **signals**, `condition()` with a quorum deadline, durable **timers**, and **activity retry policies** that absorbed a dead agent server (4 failed attempts, then success). Crash-resume after `kill -9` plus a server restart.
- **Best Use of Mastra**: an `Agent` over Gemma 4 with `createTool` tools (weather, places), `Memory` with semantic recall, and `structuredOutput` options that name the limits that shaped them, with code that drops any place the tools didn't return.
- **Best Use of MongoDB Atlas**: Atlas M0 is the agent's long-term memory (Mastra `MongoDBStore`) and its retrieval layer (**Atlas Vector Search** via `MongoDBVector`). It also stores members, plans, polls, recaps and the places cache.
- **Best Use of Render**: <DELETE THIS LINE IF NOT DEPLOYED> Render hosts the agent's API, the plan pages and `/try` on a free web service from one `render.yaml`. Its 15-minute sleep is handled by design.
- **Best Use of Gemma**: `gemma-4-26b-a4b-it` plans every outing, with native tool calls through Mastra. The 31B vs 26B comparison (validity, invented places, latency, API errors) is above.
- **Best Use of Entire**: Entire checkpoints for every agent-written commit, browsable on the `entire/checkpoints/v1` branch.

---

Quorum closes the poll at 22:00 the night before and reminds at 06:00. **If you've ever organised a group outing: where would you put the clock? The night before, or 48 hours out, so the people who can't make it say so early?**

*Built for the Hacktoberfest Open-Source AI Challenge, Week 1. Apache-2.0.*
